title.zh: 卷二 本紀第二: 太祖
title.raw: 卷二 本紀第二: 太祖 Volume 2 Annals 2: Taizu

sentences.zh: 世祖應乾興運昭德定功仁明莊孝大聖武元皇帝，諱旻，本諱阿骨打，世祖第二子也。

translations.literal: The emperor of posthumous title Shizu Yingqian Xingyun Zhaode Dinggong Renming Zhuangxiao Dasheng Wuyuan, taboo name Min, original taboo name Aguda, was Shizu’s second son.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu (Grand Ancestor)—taboo name Min, born Aguda, ennobled after death with the full title from Yingqian through Wuyuan—was the second son of Shizu (World Ancestor).

sentences.zh: 母曰翼簡皇后拏懶氏。

translations.literal: His mother was Empress Yijian, of the Nalan clan.
translations.idiomatic: His mother was Empress Yijian of the Nalan clan.

sentences.zh: 遼道宗時有五色雲氣屢出東方，大若二千斛囷倉之狀，司天孔致和竊謂人曰：「其下當生異人，建非常之事。

translations.literal: In the time of Liao Daozong, five-colored cloud vapors repeatedly appeared in the east, as large in shape as a two-thousand-hu granary bin. The astronomy official Kong Zhihe privately said to people: “Below there will be born an extraordinary man who will accomplish unprecedented affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Under Liao Daozong, iridescent clouds kept rising in the east, each swell as wide as a great granary. The court astronomer Kong Zhihe whispered to others, “A prodigy will be born beneath them and do what none have done before.

sentences.zh: 天以象告，非人力所能爲也。

translations.literal: Heaven informs by signs—it is not what human power can accomplish.”
translations.idiomatic: “Heaven speaks in omens; no mortal hand could forge this.”

sentences.zh: 」咸雍四年戊申七月一日，太祖生。

translations.literal: On the first day of the seventh month of Xianyong year four, wushen, Taizu was born.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the seventh month of Xianyong year four (1068), Taizu was born.

sentences.zh: 幼時與群兒戲，力兼數輩，舉止端重，世祖尤愛之。

translations.literal: In childhood, when playing with the group of children, his strength matched several at once; his bearing was solemn and dignified—and Shizu loved him especially.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy at play he could overpower several companions at once; his manner was already grave and steady, and Shizu favored him above the rest.

sentences.zh: 世祖與臘碚、麻產戰于野鵲水，世祖被四創，疾困，坐太祖于膝，循其發而撫之，曰：「此兒長大，吾復何憂？

translations.literal: Shizu fought Labei and Machan at Yaque River. Shizu received four wounds, was gravely ill, seated Taizu on his knee, ran his hand through his hair and stroked him, saying: “When this child grows up, what more have I to worry about?
translations.idiomatic: Shizu battled Lapai and Machan at Yaque River, took four wounds, and lay near death. He set Taizu on his knee, combed his fingers through the boy’s hair, and said, “When this one is grown, what shall I have left to fear?

sentences.zh: 」十歲，好弓矢。

translations.literal: At age ten, he loved bow and arrows.
translations.idiomatic: At ten he was devoted to bow and arrow.

sentences.zh: 甫成童，即善射。

translations.literal: As soon as he came of age, he was skilled at archery.
translations.idiomatic: Hardly past boyhood he was already a master archer.

sentences.zh: 一日，遼使坐府中，顧見太祖手持弓矢，使射群烏，連三發皆中。

translations.literal: One day a Liao envoy was seated in the hall; glancing up he saw Taizu holding bow and arrows and had him shoot at a flock of crows—three shots in succession all hit.
translations.idiomatic: Once a Liao envoy sat in the hall, looked up, and saw Taizu with bow in hand. He bade him shoot at a flight of crows; three arrows in a row found their mark.

sentences.zh: 遼使矍然曰：「奇男子也！

translations.literal: The Liao envoy started and said: “What an extraordinary youth!
translations.idiomatic: The envoy started and cried, “What a prodigy!

sentences.zh: 」太祖嘗宴紇石烈部活離罕家，散步門外，南望高阜，使衆射之，皆不能至。

translations.literal: Taizu once feasted at Huoli Khan’s home in the Heishilie division; strolling outside the gate he looked south to a high mound and had the assembly shoot at it—none could reach it.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu once feasted at Huoli Khan’s house in the Heishilie division. Walking outside the gate he looked south to a high knoll and had the company shoot at it; none could reach it.

sentences.zh: 太祖一發過之，度所至逾三百二十步。

translations.literal: Taizu with one shot passed beyond it; estimating the distance, it exceeded three hundred and twenty paces.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu’s single shaft flew past it; by measure the shot exceeded three hundred and twenty paces.

sentences.zh: 宗室謾都訶最善射遠，其不及者猶百步也。

translations.literal: Clansman Manduhu was best at shooting far; those who could not match him still fell short by a hundred paces.
translations.idiomatic: The clansman Manduhu was the finest long bow in the tribe; archers who could not equal him still fell a hundred paces short.

sentences.zh: 天德三年，立射碑以識焉。

translations.literal: In Tiande year three a shooting monument was erected to mark it.
translations.idiomatic: In Tiande year three (1115) a shooting stele was raised to mark the spot.

sentences.zh: 世祖伐卜灰，太祖因辭不失請從行，世祖不許而心異之。

translations.literal: Shizu campaigned against Buhui; Taizu through Cibushi asked to accompany the expedition—Shizu did not permit it but inwardly noted him as unusual.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizu marched on Buhui, Taizu asked Cibushi to request leave to go along. Shizu refused, yet inwardly marked him as out of the ordinary.

sentences.zh: 烏春既死，窩謀罕請和。

translations.literal: After Wuchun died, Womouhan sued for peace.
translations.idiomatic: After Wuchun’s death, Womouhan sought peace.

sentences.zh: 既請和，復來攻，遂圍其城。

translations.literal: Having sued for peace, he attacked again and thereupon besieged the city.
translations.idiomatic: No sooner had he sued for peace than he struck again and laid siege to the town.

sentences.zh: 太祖年二十三，被短甲，免胄，不介馬，行圍號令諸軍。

translations.literal: Taizu was twenty-three; he wore short armor, was bareheaded, without caparison on his horse, and went about the encirclement giving orders to the armies.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu was twenty-three. In light armor, helmet off, horse unbarded, he rode the siege line and shouted orders to the host.

sentences.zh: 城中望而識之。

translations.literal: Those in the city looked out and recognized him.
translations.idiomatic: Men on the walls looked out and knew him at once.

sentences.zh: 壯士太峪乘駿馬持槍出城，馳刺太祖。

translations.literal: A stalwart of the city, Taiyu, mounted a swift horse, took a spear, and charged out to thrust at Taizu.
translations.idiomatic: A champion named Taiyu vaulted onto a swift horse, spear in hand, and galloped out to run Taizu through.

sentences.zh: 太祖不及備，舅氏活臘胡馳出其間，擊太峪，槍折，刺中其馬，太峪僅得免。

translations.literal: Taizu had no time to prepare; his maternal uncle Huolahu galloped between them, struck Taiyu—the spear shaft broke, the point pierced his horse, and Taiyu barely escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu was caught unready; his uncle Huolahu spurred between them, struck Taiyu, snapped the spear shaft, drove the point into Taiyu’s mount, and Taiyu barely got away.

sentences.zh: 嘗與沙忽帶出營殺略，不令世祖知之。

translations.literal: He once went out of camp with Shahudai on a killing raid, not letting Shizu know.
translations.idiomatic: He once slipped from camp with Shahudai to raid and kill, keeping Shizu in the dark.

sentences.zh: 且還，敵以重兵追之。

translations.literal: When they turned back, the enemy pursued with heavy troops.
translations.idiomatic: On the return the foe came after them in strength.

sentences.zh: 獨行隘巷中，失道，追者益急。

translations.literal: Alone in a narrow lane he lost the way, and the pursuers pressed harder.
translations.idiomatic: Riding alone through a tight lane he lost the track; the pursuit closed in.

sentences.zh: 值高岸與人等，馬一躍而過，追者乃還。

translations.literal: He came to a high bank level with a man’s height; the horse leaped it in one bound and the pursuers turned back.
translations.idiomatic: He reached a bank as tall as a man; his horse cleared it in a single bound, and the pursuers gave up.

sentences.zh: 世祖寢疾，太祖以事如遼統軍司。

translations.literal: Shizu lay ill in bed; Taizu went on business to the Liao frontier command.
translations.idiomatic: While Shizu lay bedridden, Taizu went on affairs to the Liao frontier command.

sentences.zh: 將行，世祖戒之曰：「汝速了此事，五月未半而歸，則我猶及見汝也。

translations.literal: About to depart, Shizu admonished him: “Settle this matter quickly; if you return before mid-fifth month, I may yet see you.
translations.idiomatic: As he was leaving, Shizu warned him, “Finish the business swiftly—if you are back before the middle of the fifth month, I may still see you.

sentences.zh: 」太祖往見曷魯騷古統軍，既畢事，前世祖沒一日還至家。

translations.literal: Taizu went to see Commissioner Helu Saogu; when the business was done he returned home one day before Shizu died.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu called on Commissioner Helu Saogu; when the errand was done he reached home one day before Shizu’s death.

sentences.zh: 世祖見太祖來，所請事皆如志，喜甚，執太祖手，抱其頸而撫之，謂穆宗曰：「烏雅束柔善，惟此子足了契丹事。

translations.literal: Shizu saw Taizu arrive; every request had gone as he wished. Overjoyed, he took Taizu’s hand, embraced his neck and stroked him, and said to Muzong: “Wuyashu is gentle and mild—only this child can finish the Khitan affair.
translations.idiomatic: Shizu saw Taizu return; every petition had been granted as he wished. Delighted, he seized Taizu’s hand, drew him by the neck and caressed him, and told Muzong, “You are soft by nature, Wuyashu—only this boy can settle the Khitan business.

sentences.zh: 」穆宗亦雅重太祖，出入必俱。

translations.literal: Muzong too held Taizu in high esteem; going out and coming in, they were always together.
translations.idiomatic: Muzong likewise prized Taizu; in and out of doors they were never apart.

sentences.zh: 太祖遠出而歸，穆宗必親迓之。

translations.literal: When Taizu returned from a distant journey, Muzong always went in person to meet him.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Taizu came back from afar, Muzong went out himself to welcome him.

sentences.zh: 世祖已擒臘醅，麻產尚據直屋鎧水。

translations.literal: Shizu had already captured Lapai; Machan still held Zhiwu on the Kai River.
translations.idiomatic: Shizu had taken Lapai prisoner; Machan still held Zhiwu on the Kai River.

sentences.zh: 肅宗使太祖先取麻產家屬，康宗至直屋鎧水圍之。

translations.literal: Suzong sent Taizu first to seize Machan’s household; Kangzong came to Zhiwu on the Kai River and invested it.
translations.idiomatic: Suzong sent Taizu ahead to take Machan’s family; Kangzong came to Zhiwu on the Kai and laid siege.

sentences.zh: 太祖會軍，親獲麻產，獻馘于遼。

translations.literal: Taizu joined the armies, personally captured Machan, and presented the severed ears to Liao.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu united the columns, took Machan himself, and sent his severed ears to the Liao as trophy.

sentences.zh: 遼命太祖爲詳穩，仍命穆宗、辭不失、歡都皆爲詳穩。

translations.literal: The Liao appointed Taizu xiangwen, and likewise appointed Muzong, Cibushi, and Huandu all xiangwen.
translations.idiomatic: The Liao made Taizu a xiangwen (detachment commander), and Muzong, Cibushi, and Huandu xiangwen as well.

sentences.zh: 久之。

translations.literal: After a long while.
translations.idiomatic: Some time later.

sentences.zh: 以偏師伐泥厖古部跋黑、播立開等，乃以達塗阿爲鄉導，沿帥水夜行襲之，鹵其妻子。

translations.literal: With a detached force he campaigned against the Nimogu division’s Bahei, Bolikai, and the rest; he took Datu’a as guide, followed the Shuai River by night to strike them, and carried off their wives and children.
translations.idiomatic: He led a flank column against Bahei and Bolikai of the Nimogu and others, took Datu’a as guide, marched by night along the Shuai River to surprise them, and seized their wives and children.

sentences.zh: 初，溫都部跋忒殺唐括部跋葛，穆宗命太祖伐之。

translations.literal: Earlier, Bate of the Wendu division had killed Bage of the Tangguo division; Muzong ordered Taizu to campaign against him.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Bate of the Wendu had killed Bage of the Tangguo; Muzong ordered Taizu to march against him.

sentences.zh: 太祖入辭，謂穆宗曰：「昨夕見赤祥，此行必克敵。

translations.literal: Taizu entered to take leave and said to Muzong: “Last night I saw a crimson omen—on this campaign we are certain to defeat the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu came to bid farewell and told Muzong, “I saw a red sign in the night—this expedition is sure to break the foe.

sentences.zh: 」遂行。

translations.literal: Thereupon he set out.
translations.idiomatic: He set out at once.

sentences.zh: 是歲大雪，寒甚。

translations.literal: That year the snow was heavy and the cold severe.
translations.idiomatic: That year snow lay deep and the cold was brutal.

sentences.zh: 與烏古論部兵沿土溫水過末鄰鄉，追及跋忒于阿斯溫山北濼之間，殺之。

translations.literal: With Wugulun troops he followed the Tuwenshui River past Molin village, overtook Bate between the north marsh of Mount Asiwen, and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: With Wugulun warriors he tracked the Tuwenshui past Molin, ran Bate down in the north marsh by Mount Asiwen, and killed him.

sentences.zh: 軍還，穆宗親迓太祖于靄建村。

translations.literal: When the army returned, Muzong went in person to meet Taizu at Aijian village.
translations.idiomatic: On the army’s return Muzong went himself to welcome Taizu at Aijian village.

sentences.zh: 撒改以都統伐留可，謾都訶合石土門伐敵庫德。

translations.literal: Sagai as commander-in-chief campaigned against Liuke; Manduhu and Shitumen campaigned against Dikude.
translations.idiomatic: Sagai took overall command against Liuke; Manduhu and Shitumen marched on Dikude.

sentences.zh: 撒改與將佐議，或欲先平邊地部落城堡，或欲徑攻留可城，議不能決，願得太祖至軍中。

translations.literal: Sagai consulted with his generals: some wished first to pacify the border tribes’ castles, some wished to attack Liuke’s city directly—the debate could not be settled, and they wished Taizu to come to the army.
translations.idiomatic: Sagai debated with his officers—some wanted the border forts reduced first, others a straight strike at Liuke’s town—and could not decide. They asked that Taizu join the host.

sentences.zh: 穆宗使太祖往，曰：「事必有可疑。

translations.literal: Muzong sent Taizu off, saying: “In this affair there must be something doubtful.
translations.idiomatic: Muzong sent Taizu forth, saying, “Something in this campaign does not sit right.

sentences.zh: 軍之未發者止有甲士七十，盡以畀汝。

translations.literal: Of the troops not yet sent, only seventy armored men remain—give them all to you.
translations.idiomatic: Only seventy armored men are still here who have not marched—I give them all to you.

sentences.zh: 」謾都訶在米里迷石罕城下，石土門未到，土人欲執謾都訶以與敵，使來告急，遇太祖于斜堆甸。

translations.literal: Manduhu was below Milimishi Khan’s city; Shitumen had not yet arrived. The locals wished to seize Manduhu and hand him to the enemy; they sent urgent word, met Taizu at Xiedui meadow.
translations.idiomatic: Manduhu lay under Milimishi Khan’s walls; Shitumen had not come up. The townspeople meant to seize Manduhu for the foe and sent in haste—meeting Taizu at Xiedui meadow.

sentences.zh: 太祖曰：「國兵盡在此矣。

translations.literal: Taizu said: “The state’s troops are all here.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu said, “Every soldier of the state is in this body.

sentences.zh: 使敵先得志于謾都訶，後雖種誅之，何益也。

translations.literal: If the enemy first gains their aim at Mandouhe, later though we exterminate them to the last man, what use is it?
translations.idiomatic: If the enemy seizes their advantage at Mandouhe first, what good will it do us to exterminate them afterward?

sentences.zh: 」乃分甲士四十與之。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he divided forty armored soldiers and gave them to him.
translations.idiomatic: " He then sent Mandouhe forty armored men.

sentences.zh: 太祖以三十人指撒改軍。

translations.literal: The Founder took thirty men and headed toward Sagai's army.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu himself led thirty men toward Sagai's army.

sentences.zh: 道遇人曰：「敵已據盆搦嶺南路矣。

translations.literal: On the road he met someone who said: "The enemy has already seized the southern road over Pen'uo Ridge.
translations.idiomatic: On the march he met someone who said, "The enemy already holds the southern pass of Pen'uo Ridge.

sentences.zh: 」衆欲由沙偏嶺往，太祖曰：「汝等畏敵耶？

translations.literal: " The multitude wished to go by way of Shapian Ridge. The Founder said: "Do you fear the enemy?
translations.idiomatic: " The troops wanted to detour by Shapian Ridge. Taizu said, "Are you afraid of the enemy?

sentences.zh: 」既度盆搦嶺，不見敵，已而聞敵乃守沙偏嶺以拒我。

translations.literal: " Having crossed Pen'uo Ridge, they did not see the enemy; presently they heard that the enemy was in fact guarding Shapian Ridge to resist them.
translations.idiomatic: " They crossed Pen'uo Ridge and saw no enemy; soon they learned the enemy was holding Shapian Ridge to block them.

sentences.zh: 及至撒改軍，夜急攻之，遲明破其衆。

translations.literal: When they reached Sagai's army, at night they pressed the attack; at the late dawn they broke his host.
translations.idiomatic: When they joined Sagai's force they attacked at night and routed the enemy by dawn.

sentences.zh: 是時，留可、塢塔皆在遼。

translations.literal: At this time Liuke and Wuta were both in the Liao.
translations.idiomatic: Liuke and Wuta were both then at the Liao court.

sentences.zh: 既破留可，還攻塢塔城，城中人以城降。

translations.literal: Having defeated Liuke, they returned to attack Wuta city; the people in the city surrendered the city.
translations.idiomatic: After defeating Liuke they turned on Wuta's city, and its people surrendered.

sentences.zh: 初，太祖過盆搦嶺，經塢塔城下，從騎有後者，塢塔城人攻而奪之釜。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the Founder crossed Pen'uo Ridge and passed below Wuta city, some of the following horsemen lagged behind; the people of Wuta city attacked and seized their cooking pot.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Taizu had crossed Pen'uo Ridge and passed below Wuta, stragglers in his escort were set upon and robbed of their cooking pot.

sentences.zh: 太祖駐馬呼謂之曰：「毋取我炊食器。

translations.literal: The Founder halted his horse and shouted to them, saying: "Do not take my cooking vessel.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu reined in and shouted, "Do not take our cooking pots.

sentences.zh: 」其人謾言曰：「公能來此，何憂不得食。

translations.literal: " The man spoke insolently, saying: "If my lord can come here, what worry is there about not getting food?
translations.idiomatic: " The man answered insolently, "If you can come here, you need not worry about food.

sentences.zh: 」太祖以鞭指之曰：「吾破留可，即于汝乎取之。

translations.literal: " The Founder pointed his whip at him and said: "When I break Liuke, I shall take it from you.
translations.idiomatic: " Taizu pointed his whip and said, "When I defeat Liuke, I will take it from you myself.

sentences.zh: 」至是，其人持釜而前曰：「奴輩誰敢毀祥穩之器也。

translations.literal: " When it came to this, the man brought the pot forward and said: "We slaves — who would dare destroy a xiangwen vessel?
translations.idiomatic: " Now that man came forward with the pot and said, "How dare we humble ones destroy a ritual cooking vessel?

sentences.zh: 」遣蒲家奴招詐都，詐都乃降，釋之。

translations.literal: " He sent Pu Jianu to summon Zhadu; Zhadu thereupon submitted, and he released him.
translations.idiomatic: " He sent Pu Jianu to summon Zhadu, who submitted and was released.

sentences.zh: 穆宗將伐蕭海里，募兵得千餘人。

translations.literal: Muzong was about to attack Xiao Haili and raised troops, obtaining more than a thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: Muzong prepared to attack Xiao Haili and mustered more than a thousand men.

sentences.zh: 女直兵未嘗滿千，至是，太祖勇氣自倍，曰：「有此甲兵，何事不可圖也！

translations.literal: Jurchen troops had never reached a full thousand; at this time the Founder's courage doubled of itself, and he said: "With such armored soldiers, what affair cannot be plotted!
translations.idiomatic: Jurchen armies had never before reached a thousand; Taizu's courage doubled. He said, "With arms like these, what cannot we accomplish!

sentences.zh: 」海里來戰，與遼兵合，因止遼人，自爲戰。

translations.literal: " Haili came to fight and joined with Liao troops; the Founder thereupon stopped the Liao men and fought on his own.
translations.idiomatic: " Haili met them in battle alongside Liao troops; Taizu held the Liao forces back and fought alone.

sentences.zh: 勃海留守以甲贈太祖，太祖亦不受。

translations.literal: The Bohai frontier commander presented armor to the Founder as a gift, but the Founder likewise would not accept it.
translations.idiomatic: The Bohai garrison commander offered Taizu armor as a gift, but he would not take it.

sentences.zh: 穆宗問何爲不受？

translations.literal: Muzong asked why he would not accept it.
translations.idiomatic: Muzong asked why he refused.

sentences.zh: 曰：「被彼甲而戰，戰勝則是因彼成功也。

translations.literal: He said: "If I wear their armor and fight, victory would mean succeeding through them.
translations.idiomatic: He said, "If I wore their armor and won, the victory would be theirs, not ours.

sentences.zh: 」穆宗末年，令諸部不得擅置信牌馳驛訊事，號令自此始一，皆自太祖啟之。

translations.literal: " In Muzong's later years he ordered that the various tribes must not on their own authority establish trust tokens to dispatch couriers and conduct inquiries — from this time commands began to be unified, and all was initiated by the Founder.
translations.idiomatic: " In Muzong's last years he forbade tribes from issuing their own courier tokens and sending riders on private business — from then on authority was centralized, and Taizu had been the first to press for it.

sentences.zh: 康宗七年，歲不登，民多流莩，強者轉而爲盜。

translations.literal: In Kangzong's seventh year the harvest failed; the people mostly wandered famished, and the strong turned to becoming bandits.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Kangzong famine struck; refugees filled the roads, and the strong turned bandit.

sentences.zh: 歡都等欲重其法，爲盜者皆殺之。

translations.literal: Huandu and others wished to make the law heavier and executed all who became robbers.
translations.idiomatic: Huandu and others wanted harsher penalties and would have executed every thief.

sentences.zh: 太祖曰：「以財殺人，不可！

translations.literal: The Founder said: "To kill people over property — that cannot be done!
translations.idiomatic: Taizu said, "You cannot kill men for property!

sentences.zh: 財者，人所致也。

translations.literal: Property is something people produce.
translations.idiomatic: Property is only what people make.

sentences.zh: 」遂減盜賊征償法爲征三倍。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he reduced the thieves' restitution law to a levy of triple.
translations.idiomatic: " He reduced the thieves' restitution rule from capital punishment to a fine of threefold restitution.

sentences.zh: 民間多逋負，賣妻子不能償，康宗與官屬會議，太祖在外庭以帛系杖端，麾其衆，令曰：「今貧者不能自活，賣妻子以償債。

translations.literal: Among the people many were in arrears; selling wives and children they still could not repay. Kangzong was in council with his officials; the Founder, in the outer courtyard, tied silk to the end of a staff, waved his multitude, and commanded, saying: "Now the poor cannot support themselves and sell wives and children to repay debts.
translations.idiomatic: Many commoners were deep in debt and sold wives and children without clearing what they owed. While Kangzong met with his officers, Taizu stood in the outer court with silk tied to his staff, rallied the people, and proclaimed, "The poor cannot live and are selling their wives and children to pay debts.

sentences.zh: 骨肉之愛，人心所同。

translations.literal: Love of flesh and bone — all hearts share it.
translations.idiomatic: The bond of kin is the same in every heart.

sentences.zh: 自今三年勿征，過三年徐圖之。

translations.literal: From now for three years do not levy; after three years gradually plan it.
translations.idiomatic: Collect nothing for three years; after that we may collect gradually.

sentences.zh: 」衆皆聽令，聞者感泣，自是遠近歸心焉。

translations.literal: " All obeyed the order; those who heard wept with emotion, and from this time near and far gave their hearts.
translations.idiomatic: " All assented; hearers wept, and from that day loyalty spread far and wide.

sentences.zh: 歲癸巳十月，康宗夢逐狼，屢發不能中，太祖前射中之。

translations.literal: In the year guisi, in the tenth month, Kangzong dreamed of chasing a wolf; he shot many times but could not hit it; the Founder stepped forward and shot it.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of guisi, Kangzong dreamed he was chasing a wolf and could not hit it; Taizu stepped forward and struck it down.

sentences.zh: 旦日，以所夢問僚佐，衆曰：「吉。

translations.literal: At dawn the next day he asked his aides about the dream; the multitude said: "Auspicious.
translations.idiomatic: The next morning he asked his advisers about the dream; they said, "A good omen.

sentences.zh: 兄不能得而弟得之之兆也。

translations.literal: The sign that the elder brother could not obtain it but the younger brother will obtain it.
translations.idiomatic: It means the elder brother could not attain it and the younger will."

sentences.zh: 」是月，康宗即世，太祖襲位爲都勃極烈。

translations.literal: " That month Kangzong died; the Founder succeeded to the position and became Chief Jurchen Chieftain (du bojilie).
translations.idiomatic: " That month Kangzong died and Taizu succeeded him as chief chieftain (du bojilie).

sentences.zh: 遼使阿息保來，曰：「何以不告喪？

translations.literal: A Liao envoy, Ashibao, came and said: "Why did you not announce the mourning?
translations.idiomatic: The Liao envoy Ashibao came and demanded, "Why did you not report the death?

sentences.zh: 」太祖曰：「有喪不能吊，而乃以爲罪乎？

translations.literal: " The Founder said: "When there is mourning and you cannot come to condole — and yet you make it a crime?
translations.idiomatic: " Taizu replied, "You could not come to mourn — and you call that a crime?

sentences.zh: 」他日，阿息保復來，徑騎至康宗殯所，閱賵馬，欲取之。

translations.literal: " Another day Ashibao came again, rode straight to Kangzong's mourning place, inspected the funeral tribute horses, and wished to take them.
translations.idiomatic: " Another day Ashibao rode straight to Kangzong's burial place, inspected the funeral horses offered in tribute, and tried to take them.

sentences.zh: 太祖怒，將殺之，宗雄諫而止。

translations.literal: The Founder was angry and was about to kill him; Zongxiong remonstrated and he stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu was enraged and was about to kill him, but Zongxiong dissuaded him.

sentences.zh: 既而遼命久不至。

translations.literal: After a time Liao orders long did not arrive.
translations.idiomatic: For a long time after that no orders came from the Liao court.

sentences.zh: 遼主好畋獵、淫酗，怠于政事，四方奏事，往往不見省。

translations.literal: The Liao sovereign loved hunting and dissolute drinking, was slack in government affairs; memorials from the four quarters were often not reviewed.
translations.idiomatic: The Liao emperor hunted and drank to excess, neglected government, and seldom read memorials from the realm.

sentences.zh: 紇石烈阿疏既奔遼，穆宗取其城及其部衆，不能歸。

translations.literal: Hesilie Ashu had already fled to the Liao; Muzong took his city and his tribal multitude but could not return them.
translations.idiomatic: After Hesilie Ashu had fled to Liao, Muzong seized his city and followers but could not recover them.

sentences.zh: 遂與族弟銀朮可、辭里罕陰結南江居人渾都僕速，欲與俱亡入高麗。

translations.literal: Ashu then secretly joined with his clansman Yin'aike, Cilihan, and Hundu Pusu, a man dwelling on the South River, wishing together to flee into Goryeo.
translations.idiomatic: He then secretly conspired with his kinsmen Yin'aike and Cilihan and with Hundu Pusu, who lived south of the river, to flee together into Goryeo.

sentences.zh: 事覺，太祖使夾古撒喝捕之，而銀朮可、辭里罕先爲遼戍所獲，渾都僕速已亡去，撒喝取其妻子而還。

translations.literal: The affair was discovered; the Founder sent Jiagu Sahuo to seize them, but Yin'aike and Cilihan had already been captured by Liao garrison troops, Hundu Pusu had already fled, and Sahuo took their wives and children and returned.
translations.idiomatic: When the plot was exposed Taizu sent Jiagu Sahuo to arrest them, but Yin'aike and Cilihan had already been taken by Liao border troops and Hundu Pusu had escaped; Sahuo brought back only their families.

sentences.zh: 二年甲午六月，太祖至江西，遼使使來致襲節度之命。

translations.literal: In the second year jiawu, sixth month, the Founder reached Jiangxi; the Liao dispatched envoys to convey the order of succession to the military commission.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the second year, jiawu, Taizu reached the Western River district, and Liao envoys arrived to confirm his succession to the frontier command.

sentences.zh: 初，遼每歲遣使市名鷹海東青于海上，道出境內，使者貪縱，征索無藝，公私厭苦之。

translations.literal: Initially, each year the Liao sent envoys to purchase famous hawks and sea eagles (haitongqing) on the sea; the route passed through the interior, and the envoys were greedy and unrestrained, levying demands without limit — public and private alike were wearied and distressed.
translations.idiomatic: Each year the Liao sent men to buy prized sea eagles on the coast; the route crossed Jurchen lands, and the envoys extorted without limit until nobles and commoners alike were sick of them.

sentences.zh: 康宗嘗以不遣阿疏爲言，稍拒其使者。

translations.literal: Kangzong had once made an issue of not sending back Ashu and slightly resisted their envoys.
translations.idiomatic: Kangzong had already resisted Liao envoys over the refusal to return Ashu.

sentences.zh: 太祖嗣節度，亦遣蒲家奴往索阿疏，故常以此二者爲言，終至于滅遼然後已。

translations.literal: When the Founder succeeded to the commission he also sent Pu Jianu to demand Ashu; therefore these two matters were constantly raised as grievances, only ending when the Liao was destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu took command he too sent Pu Jianu to demand Ashu; these two grievances would be cited again and again until the Liao was destroyed.

sentences.zh: 至是，復遣宗室習古乃、完顏銀朮可往索阿疏。

translations.literal: At this time he again sent kinsmen Xigunai and Wanyan Yin'aike to demand Ashu.
translations.idiomatic: Now he again sent his kinsman Xigunai and Wanyan Yin'aike to demand Ashu.

sentences.zh: 習古乃等還，具言遼主驕肆廢弛之狀。

translations.literal: When Xigunai and the others returned, they fully reported the condition of the Liao sovereign — arrogant, dissolute, and slack.
translations.idiomatic: When Xigunai returned he described in full how arrogant, dissolute, and slack the Liao emperor had become.

sentences.zh: 于是召官僚耆舊，以伐遼告之，使備沖要，建城堡，修戎器，以聽後命。

translations.literal: Thereupon he summoned officials and elders of old, informed them of the campaign against Liao, and ordered them to guard strategic passes, build fortresses, and repair weapons, to await later orders.
translations.idiomatic: He then summoned officials and senior clansmen, announced the war against Liao, and ordered them to secure key passes, build forts, and ready arms, pending his further command.

sentences.zh: 遼統軍司聞之，使節度使捏哥來問狀，曰：「汝等有異志乎？

translations.literal: The Liao frontier command heard of it and sent the military commissioner Niege to inquire, saying: "Do you harbor rebellious intentions?
translations.idiomatic: When the Liao frontier command heard of this, they sent Commissioner Niege to investigate, asking, "Are you plotting rebellion?

sentences.zh: 修戰具，傷守備，將以誰禦？

translations.literal: You repair war gear and weaken defenses—against whom do you mean to defend?"
translations.idiomatic: You are arming for war and stripping your garrisons—whom do you expect to fight?"

sentences.zh: 」太祖答之曰：「設險自守，又何問哉！

translations.literal: Taizu answered: "We fortify defenses to protect ourselves—why ask?!"
translations.idiomatic: Taizu replied, "We are fortifying our borders for self-defense—why question that?!"

sentences.zh: 」遼復遣阿息保來詰之。

translations.literal: Liao again sent Ashibao to cross-examine him.
translations.idiomatic: The Liao then sent Ashibao to press him again.

sentences.zh: 太祖謂之曰：「我小國也，事大國不敢廢禮。

translations.literal: Taizu said to him: "We are a small state; in serving the great state we dare not neglect ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu told him, "We are a small people who have always observed every courtesy owed a great power.

sentences.zh: 大國德澤不施，而逋逃是主，以此字小，能無望乎？

translations.literal: The great state spreads its virtue nowhere yet harbors fugitives—on this account can our small state have no grounds to hope?
translations.idiomatic: Yet you show us no grace while sheltering our fugitives—do you think a small state has nothing to hope for?

sentences.zh: 若以阿疏與我，請事朝貢。

translations.literal: If you hand Ashu over to us, we will continue tributary service.
translations.idiomatic: Hand Ashu back and we will resume tribute as before.

sentences.zh: 苟不獲已，豈能束手受制也。

translations.literal: If that cannot be obtained, how could we bind our hands and submit to control?"
translations.idiomatic: If you refuse, we cannot simply fold our hands and submit."

sentences.zh: 」阿息保還，遼人始爲備，命統軍蕭撻不野調諸軍于甯江州。

translations.literal: Ashibao returned; the Liao then made preparations and ordered the commander Xiao Tabuye to mobilize armies at Ningjiang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Ashibao returned, the Liao began to prepare in earnest, ordering Commander Xiao Tabuye to concentrate troops at Ningjiang.

sentences.zh: 太祖聞之，使僕聒剌復索阿疏，實觀其形勢。

translations.literal: Taizu heard and sent Pula Ci again to demand Ashu, in truth to observe their military situation.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing this, Taizu sent Pula Ci once more to demand Ashu, but in fact to scout their strength.

sentences.zh: 僕聒剌還言：「遼兵多，不知其數。

translations.literal: Pula Ci returned saying: "Liao troops are many; their number is unknown."
translations.idiomatic: Pula Ci reported back, "The Liao forces are vast—we could not count them."

sentences.zh: 」太祖曰：「彼初調兵，豈能遽集如此。

translations.literal: Taizu said: "They have only begun mobilizing—how could they assemble so quickly?"
translations.idiomatic: Taizu said, "They have only just begun to mobilize—how could they already be so numerous?"

sentences.zh: 」復遣胡沙保往，還言：「惟四院統軍司與甯江州軍及渤海八百人耳。

translations.literal: He again sent Husabao; he returned saying: "Only the Four Divisions command, the Ningjiang garrison, and eight hundred Bohai troops."
translations.idiomatic: He sent Husabao next, who returned saying, "There are only the Four Divisions command, the Ningjiang garrison, and eight hundred Bohai soldiers."

sentences.zh: 」太祖曰：「果如吾言。

translations.literal: Taizu said: "It is indeed as I said."
translations.idiomatic: Taizu said, "Just as I said."

sentences.zh: 」謂諸將佐曰：「遼人知我將舉兵，集諸路軍備我，我必先發制之，無爲人制。

translations.literal: He told the generals and aides: "The Liao know we mean to raise troops and are gathering armies from all routes to prepare against us—we must strike first and seize the initiative, not let others control us."
translations.idiomatic: He told his commanders, "The Liao know we are about to march and are mustering troops on every road against us. We must strike first and seize the initiative—not wait to be pinned down."

sentences.zh: 」衆皆曰：「善。

translations.literal: All said: "Good."
translations.idiomatic: All agreed that this was right.

sentences.zh: 」乃入見宣靖皇后，告以伐遼事。

translations.literal: He then went in to see Empress Xuanjing and told her of the campaign against Liao.
translations.idiomatic: He went in to see Empress Xuanjing and told her of the campaign against Liao.

sentences.zh: 后曰：「汝嗣父兄立邦家，見可則行。

translations.literal: The empress said: "You succeeded your father and elder brothers in founding the state; when you see an opening, act.
translations.idiomatic: The empress said, "You inherited your father and brothers' work in building this realm—when you see your chance, act.

sentences.zh: 吾老矣，無貽我憂，汝必不至是也。

translations.literal: I am old—do not cause me worry; you would never go so far as that."
translations.idiomatic: I am old; do not burden me with grief—you would never go too far."

sentences.zh: 」太祖感泣，奉觴爲壽。

translations.literal: Taizu wept with emotion and raised a cup to wish her long life.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu wept and raised a cup to wish her long life.

sentences.zh: 即奉后率諸將出門，舉觴東向，以遼人荒肆，不歸阿疏，並己用兵之意，禱于皇天后土。

translations.literal: At once he led the empress and generals outside the gate, raised a cup facing east, and prayed to Heaven and Earth, citing the Liao's lawless excesses, their refusal to return Ashu, and his own intent to use force.
translations.idiomatic: At once he led the empress and his generals outside, raised a cup toward the east, and prayed to Heaven and Earth—citing the Liao's lawlessness, their refusal to return Ashu, and his resolve to take up arms.

sentences.zh: 酹畢，后命太祖正坐，與僚屬會酒，號令諸部。

translations.literal: When the libation was finished the empress ordered Taizu to take the seat of honor, drink with his officers, and issue orders to all divisions.
translations.idiomatic: When the libation was done, the empress seated Taizu in the place of honor, shared wine with his officers, and had him issue orders to every division.

sentences.zh: 使婆盧火征移懶路迪古乃兵，斡魯古、阿魯撫諭斡忽、急賽兩路系遼籍女直，實不迭往完睹路執遼障鷹官達魯古部副使辭列、甯江州渤海大家奴。

translations.literal: He sent Boluhuo to campaign against the Dirgunen troops of the Yilan route, Wulugu and Alu to pacify the Wahu and Jisai routes of Jurchen registered under Liao, and Sabudie to the Wandu route to seize the Liao hawk-blocking official of the Dalugu tribe, Deputy Commissioner Cilie, and the Bohai headsmen of Ningjiang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Boluhuo against the Dirgunen levies on the Yilan circuit, Wulugu and Alu to win over Jurchen on the Wahu and Jisai routes still on Liao rolls, and Sabudie to the Wandu circuit to arrest the Liao hawking commissioner of the Dalugu tribe, Deputy Commissioner Cilie, and the Bohai headmen at Ningjiang.

sentences.zh: 于是達魯古部實里館來告曰：「聞舉兵伐遼，我部誰從？

translations.literal: Thereupon the Shili lodge of the Dalugu tribe came to report: "We hear you are raising troops against Liao—which side shall our tribe follow?"
translations.idiomatic: Then envoys from the Shili lodge of the Dalugu tribe came asking, "We hear you are marching against Liao—which side should our clan take?"

sentences.zh: 」太祖曰：「吾兵雖少，舊國也，與汝鄰境，固當從我。

translations.literal: Taizu said: "Though our troops are few, this is the old homeland and borders your territory—you should naturally follow me.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu said, "Our army is small, but this is the ancestral land and borders yours—you should stand with us.

sentences.zh: 若畏遼人，自往就之。」

translations.literal: If you fear the Liao, go join them yourselves."
translations.idiomatic: If you fear the Liao, go submit to them on your own."

sentences.zh: 九月，太祖進軍甯江州，次寥晦城。

translations.literal: In the ninth month Taizu advanced on Ningjiang Prefecture and encamped at Liaohui city.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Taizu marched on Ningjiang and halted at Liaohui.

sentences.zh: 婆盧火徵兵後期，杖之，復遣督軍。

translations.literal: Boluhuo was late in levying troops; he was flogged and again sent to press the army forward.
translations.idiomatic: Boluhuo was late raising his levies; Taizu had him beaten and sent him back to hurry the troops.

sentences.zh: 諸路兵皆會于來流水，得二千五百人。

translations.literal: Troops from all routes assembled at the Lailiu River, totaling two thousand five hundred men.
translations.idiomatic: Forces from every route gathered on the Lailiu River—two thousand five hundred men in all.

sentences.zh: 致遼之罪，申告于天地曰：「世事遼國，恪修職貢，定烏春、窩謀罕之亂，破蕭海里之衆，有功不省，而侵侮是加。

translations.literal: Setting forth Liao's crimes, he declared to Heaven and Earth: "We have served the Liao state, diligently maintaining tribute and office, quelled the rebellions of Wuchun and Womohan, and defeated Xiao Haili's host—yet our merits went unrecognized while insults were heaped upon us.
translations.idiomatic: He laid out the Liao's crimes before Heaven and Earth: "We served the Liao faithfully, paid tribute, put down the revolts of Wuchun and Womohan, and broke Xiao Haili's army—yet our service went unrewarded and insult was piled on insult.

sentences.zh: 罪人阿疏，屢請不遣。

translations.literal: The criminal Ashu was repeatedly requested but not sent back.
translations.idiomatic: The fugitive Ashu we asked for again and again, and you would not return him.

sentences.zh: 今將問罪于遼，天地其鑒佑之。

translations.literal: Now we will call Liao to account—may Heaven and Earth witness and aid us."
translations.idiomatic: Today we march to punish the Liao—may Heaven and Earth witness and aid us."

sentences.zh: 」遂命諸將傳挺而誓曰：「汝等同心盡力，有功者，奴婢部曲爲良，庶人官之，先有官者敘進，輕重視功。

translations.literal: He then ordered the generals to pass a club and swear: "You shall join hearts and exert your strength. Those with merit—bondservants and household troops become commoners, commoners receive office, those already in office advance in rank, light and heavy reward according to merit.
translations.idiomatic: He had his commanders pass a club and swear: "Fight as one. Those who merit reward—bondsmen and household troops will be freed, commoners will be given office, officers will advance by rank, and rewards will match the deed.

sentences.zh: 苟違誓言，身死梃下，家屬無赦。

translations.literal: If you violate this oath, die beneath the club, and your families shall not be spared."
translations.idiomatic: Break this oath and you die by the club, and your families will not be spared."

sentences.zh: 」師次唐括帶斡甲之地，諸軍禳射，介而立，有光如烈火，起于人足及戈矛之上，人以爲兵祥。

translations.literal: The army halted at Tangkuo Daiwogua; the troops performed exorcistic archery and stood armored. A light like blazing fire rose from men's feet and atop spears and halberds—people took it as an omen of victory.
translations.idiomatic: The army halted at Tangkuo Daiwogua. The troops performed ritual archery in armor, and a blaze-like light rose from their feet and weapons—taken as a sign of victory.

sentences.zh: 明日，次紮只水，光見如初。

translations.literal: The next day they halted at the Zhazhi River; the light appeared as before.
translations.idiomatic: The next day they camped on the Zhazhi River, and the same light appeared again.

sentences.zh: 將至遼界，先使宗幹督士卒夷塹。

translations.literal: As they were about to reach the Liao border, he first sent Zonggan to supervise the troops in leveling ditches.
translations.idiomatic: Before crossing into Liao territory, he sent Zonggan ahead to fill in the ditches.

sentences.zh: 既度遇渤海軍攻我左翼七謀克，衆少卻，敵兵直犯中軍。

translations.literal: After crossing they met Bohai troops attacking our left-wing seven mouke; our numbers were few and we gave ground, and the enemy drove straight at the center army.
translations.idiomatic: Once across, Bohai troops struck the left wing's seven mouke. Outnumbered, our men fell back as the enemy drove straight for the center.

sentences.zh: 斜也出戰，哲垤先驅。

translations.literal: Xieye went out to fight; Zhedie rode in the vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: Xieye rode out to fight, with Zhedie in the lead.

sentences.zh: 太祖曰：「戰不可易也。

translations.literal: Taizu said: "In battle one must not change position lightly."
translations.idiomatic: Taizu said, "In battle you must not shift your ground lightly."

sentences.zh: 」遣宗幹止之。

translations.literal: He sent Zonggan to stop them.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Zonggan to rein them in.

sentences.zh: 宗幹馳出斜也前，控止哲垤馬，斜也遂與俱還。

translations.literal: Zonggan galloped out before Xieye, seized Zhedie's bridle, and Xieye then returned with him.
translations.idiomatic: Zonggan galloped ahead of Xieye, caught Zhedie's bridle, and both turned back.

sentences.zh: 敵人從之，耶律謝十墜馬，遼人前救。

translations.literal: The enemy pursued; Yelü Sheshi fell from his horse, and Liao troops rushed forward to rescue him.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy pursued. Yelü Sheshi was thrown from his horse, and Liao riders rushed to save him.

sentences.zh: 太祖射救者斃。

translations.literal: Taizu shot the rescuer dead.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu shot the rescuer dead.

sentences.zh: 並射謝十中之。

translations.literal: He also shot Sheshi and hit him.
translations.idiomatic: He struck Sheshi as well.

sentences.zh: 有騎突前，又射之，徹紮洞胸。

translations.literal: A rider charged forward; he shot again, the arrow piercing clean through the chest.
translations.idiomatic: Another rider charged; Taizu shot again, the arrow punching clear through his chest.

sentences.zh: 謝十拔箭走，追射之，中其背，飲矢之半，僨而死，獲所乘馬。

translations.literal: Sheshi pulled out the arrow and fled; pursuing, Taizu shot him in the back—the arrow sank halfway in—and he fell dead; they captured his horse.
translations.idiomatic: Sheshi pulled out the arrow and fled. Taizu chased him down with a shot in the back—the shaft sank halfway in—and Sheshi fell dead. They took his horse.

sentences.zh: 宗幹與數騎陷遼軍中，太祖救之，免胄戰。

translations.literal: Zonggan and several riders were trapped in the Liao army; Taizu rescued them, fighting bareheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Zonggan and a few riders were trapped in the Liao lines. Taizu fought in to save them, helmet off.

sentences.zh: 或自傍射之，矢拂于顙。

translations.literal: Someone shot at him from the side; an arrow grazed his forehead.
translations.idiomatic: An arrow from the flank grazed his brow.

sentences.zh: 太祖顧見射者，一矢而斃。

translations.literal: Taizu turned, saw the shooter, and dropped him with one arrow.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu spotted the archer and dropped him with a single shot.

sentences.zh: 謂將士曰：「盡敵而止。

translations.literal: He told the officers and men: "Fight until the enemy is spent, then stop."
translations.idiomatic: He told his men, "Fight until the enemy is spent—then stop."

sentences.zh: 」衆從之，勇氣自倍。

translations.literal: The host obeyed, and their courage doubled of itself.
translations.idiomatic: They obeyed, and their courage doubled.

sentences.zh: 敵大奔，相蹂踐死者十七八。

translations.literal: The enemy fled in great disorder; seven or eight in ten died trampled underfoot.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy broke and ran; seven or eight in ten were trampled to death in the rout.

sentences.zh: 撒改在別路，不及會戰，使人以戰勝告之，而以謝十馬賜之。

translations.literal: Sagai was on another route and did not reach the battle; someone was sent to tell him of the victory, and Sheshi's horse was given to him as a gift.
translations.idiomatic: Sagai was on another route and missed the battle; a messenger brought him word of the victory and the gift of Sheshi's horse.

sentences.zh: 撒改使其子宗翰、完顏希尹來賀，且稱帝，因勸進。

translations.literal: Sagai sent his sons Zonghan and Wanyan Xiyin to offer congratulations, proclaim him emperor, and urge him to ascend the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Sagai sent his sons Zonghan and Wanyan Xiyin to congratulate him, hail him as emperor, and urge him to take the throne.

sentences.zh: 太祖曰：「一戰而勝，遂稱大號，何示人淺也。

translations.literal: Taizu said: "To win one battle and then assume the great title—how shallow that would appear to others."
translations.idiomatic: Taizu said, "To proclaim an imperial title after a single victory—what a shallow show that would make."

sentences.zh: 」進軍甯江州，諸軍填塹攻城。

translations.literal: He advanced on Ningjiang Prefecture; the armies filled ditches and assaulted the city.
translations.idiomatic: He marched on Ningjiang, and his troops filled the ditches and stormed the walls.

sentences.zh: 甯江人自東門出，溫蒂痕、阿徒罕邀擊，盡殪之。

translations.literal: The people of Ningjiang came out from the east gate; Wendihen and Atuhan intercepted and annihilated them all.
translations.idiomatic: The garrison sallied from the east gate; Wendihen and Atuhan cut them off and killed them to the last man.

sentences.zh: 十月朔，克其城，獲防禦使大藥師奴，陰縱之，使招諭遼人。

translations.literal: On the first day of the tenth month they took the city, captured the defense commissioner Dayaoshinu, secretly released him, and had him summon and persuade the Liao people.
translations.idiomatic: On the first of the tenth month the city fell. They took Defense Commissioner Dayaoshinu, secretly released him, and sent him to win over the Liao garrisons.

sentences.zh: 鐵驪部來送款。

translations.literal: The Tieli tribe came to offer submission.
translations.idiomatic: The Tieli tribe submitted.

sentences.zh: 次來流城，以俘獲賜將士。

translations.literal: They halted at Lailiu city and distributed captives and booty among the officers and men.
translations.idiomatic: They camped at Lailiu and divided the spoils among the troops.

sentences.zh: 召渤海梁福、斡答剌使之偽亡去，招諭其鄉人曰：「女直、渤海本同一家，我興師伐罪，不濫及無辜也。

translations.literal: He summoned the Bohai Liang Fu and Wodala and had them feign flight, to summon and persuade their countrymen, saying: "Jurchen and Bohai were originally one family. I raise troops to punish crime and do not harm the innocent indiscriminately."
translations.idiomatic: He sent the Bohai Liang Fu and Wodala to pretend desertion and tell their people, "Jurchen and Bohai are one family. I march to punish wrongdoers, not to harm the innocent."

sentences.zh: 」使完顏婁室招諭系遼籍女直。

translations.literal: He sent Wanyan Loushi to summon and persuade Jurchen registered under Liao.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Wanyan Loushi to win over Jurchen still on Liao rolls.

sentences.zh: 師還，謁宣靖皇后，以所獲頒宗室耆老，以實里館貲產給將士。

translations.literal: The army returned; he paid respects to Empress Xuanjing, distributed the spoils among the imperial clan and elders, and gave the Shili lodge's property to the officers and men.
translations.idiomatic: The army returned. Taizu paid respects to Empress Xuanjing, shared the booty with the clan elders, and gave the Shili lodge's estates to his troops.

sentences.zh: 初命諸路以三百戶爲謀克，十謀克爲猛安。

translations.literal: For the first time he ordered all routes to organize three hundred households as a mouke and ten mouke as a meng'an.
translations.idiomatic: For the first time he ordered every circuit to group three hundred households into a mouke and ten mouke into a meng'an.

sentences.zh: 酬斡等撫定讒謀水女直。

translations.literal: Chouwo and others pacified the Jurchen of the Chanmou River.
translations.idiomatic: Chouwo and others pacified the Jurchen along the Chanmou River.

sentences.zh: 鱉古酋長胡蘇魯以城降。

translations.literal: Chief Husulu of Biegu surrendered his city.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Husulu of Biegu surrendered his town.

sentences.zh: 十一月，遼都統蕭糺里、副都統撻不野將步騎十萬會于鴨子河北。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month Liao Commander-in-Chief Xiao Jiuli and Vice Commander Tabuye led one hundred thousand infantry and cavalry to assemble north of the Yazi River.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month Liao Commander Xiao Jiuli and Vice Commander Tabuye massed a hundred thousand foot and horse north of the Yazi River.

sentences.zh: 太祖自將擊之。

translations.literal: Taizu personally led the attack against them.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu led the counterattack in person.

sentences.zh: 未至鴨子河，既夜，太祖方就枕，若有扶其首者三，寤而起，曰：「神明警我也！

translations.literal: Before reaching the Yazi River, at night Taizu was about to sleep when something seemed to lift his head three times; he awoke and rose, saying: "The spirits warn me!"
translations.idiomatic: Before they reached the Yazi, Taizu had lain down for the night when something seemed to lift his head three times. He woke and said, "The spirits are warning me!"

sentences.zh: 」即鳴鼓舉燧而行。

translations.literal: At once he beat drums, raised beacon fires, and marched.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the drums beaten, the signal fires lit, and the army moved out at once.

sentences.zh: 黎明及河，遼兵方壞淩道，選壯士十輩擊走之。

translations.literal: At dawn they reached the river; Liao troops were destroying the pontoon bridge. He chose ten stalwart warriors who drove them off.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn they reached the river as Liao troops were breaking up the pontoon bridge. Ten picked warriors drove them off.

sentences.zh: 大軍繼進，遂登岸。

translations.literal: The main army followed and crossed to the north bank.
translations.idiomatic: The main force followed and gained the north bank.

sentences.zh: 甲士三千七百，至者才三之一。

translations.literal: Armored soldiers numbered three thousand seven hundred, but only one in three had arrived.
translations.idiomatic: Of thirty-seven hundred armored men, only a third had yet come up.

sentences.zh: 俄與敵遇于出河店，會大風起，塵埃蔽天，乘風勢擊之，遼兵潰。

translations.literal: Soon they met the enemy at Chuhe post; a great wind arose and dust blotted out the sky. Riding the wind they struck, and the Liao army collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: They soon met the enemy at Chuhe post. A fierce wind rose, dust blotted out the sky, and they struck with the gale at their backs. The Liao army broke.

sentences.zh: 逐至斡論濼，殺獲首虜及車馬甲兵珍玩不可勝計，遍賜官屬將士，燕犒彌日。

translations.literal: They pursued to Wolun Marsh; killed and captured, heads, prisoners, horses, chariots, armor, and precious objects beyond counting were distributed throughout to officials and soldiers, and feasting lasted many days.
translations.idiomatic: The pursuit ran to Wolun Marsh. Heads, prisoners, horses, armor, and treasure beyond counting were shared among officers and men, and the victory feast lasted for days.

sentences.zh: 遼人嘗言女直兵若滿萬則不可敵，至是始滿萬雲。

translations.literal: The Liao had once said that if Jurchen troops reached ten thousand they could not be withstood; only now did they reach ten thousand, it was said.
translations.idiomatic: The Liao had long said that ten thousand Jurchen warriors could not be stopped—only now, it was said, had that number been reached.

sentences.zh: 斡魯古敗遼兵，斬其節度使撻不野。

translations.literal: Wulugu defeated Liao troops and beheaded their military commissioner Tabuye.
translations.idiomatic: Wulugu routed a Liao force and killed Commissioner Tabuye.

sentences.zh: 僕虺等攻賓州，拔之。

translations.literal: Puhui and others attacked Bin Prefecture and took it.
translations.idiomatic: Puhui and others took Bin Prefecture by assault.

sentences.zh: 兀惹雛鶻室來降。

translations.literal: Wunai Chuguishi came to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Wunai Chuguishi submitted.

sentences.zh: 遼將赤狗兒戰于賓州，僕虺、渾黜敗之。

translations.literal: The Liao general Chigou'er fought at Bin Prefecture; Puhui and Hunchu defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: The Liao general Chigou'er fought at Bin; Puhui and Hunchu defeated him.

sentences.zh: 鐵驪王回離保以所部降。

translations.literal: The Tieli king Huilibao surrendered with his following.
translations.idiomatic: The Tieli king Huilibao surrendered with his followers.

sentences.zh: 吾睹補、蒲察復敗赤狗兒、蕭乙薛軍于祥州東。

translations.literal: Wudubu and Pucha again defeated the armies of Chigou'er and Xiao Yixue east of Xiang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Wudubu and Pucha again defeated Chigou'er and Xiao Yixue east of Xiang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 斡忽、急塞兩路降。

translations.literal: The Wahu and Jisai routes surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: The Wahu and Jisai circuits submitted.

sentences.zh: 斡魯古敗遼軍于鹹州西，斬統軍實婁于陣。

translations.literal: Wulugu defeated Liao troops west of Xian Prefecture and beheaded Commander-in-Chief Shilou in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Wulugu routed the Liao west of Xian Prefecture and killed Commander Shilou in the field.

sentences.zh: 完顏婁室克鹹州。

translations.literal: Wanyan Loushi captured Xian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Wanyan Loushi took Xian Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 是月，吳乞買、撒改、辭不失率宮屬諸將勸進，願以新歲元日恭上尊號，太祖不許。

translations.literal: That month Wuqimai, Sagai, and Cibushi led palace kin and generals in urging him to advance, wishing to respectfully offer the exalted title on New Year's Day of the new year; Taizu did not consent.
translations.idiomatic: That month Wuqimai, Sagai, and Cibushi led the imperial kin and commanders in urging him to take the throne, proposing to invest him on New Year's Day—Taizu refused.

sentences.zh: 阿離合懣、蒲家奴、宗翰等進曰：「今大功已建，若不稱號，無以系天下心。

translations.literal: Alihemen, Pu Jianu, Zonghan, and others advanced saying: "Great merit is now achieved; if you do not assume a title, there is no means to bind the hearts of the realm."
translations.idiomatic: Alihemen, Pu Jianu, Zonghan, and others pressed him: "Your great work is done—without a title you cannot hold the realm's loyalty."

sentences.zh: 」太祖曰：「吾將思之。」

translations.literal: Taizu said: "I will consider it."
translations.idiomatic: Taizu said, "I will think on it."

sentences.zh: 收國元年正月壬申朔，群臣奉上尊號。

translations.literal: On the first day renshen of the first month of the first year of Shouguo, the ministers presented the exalted title.
translations.idiomatic: On New Year's Day of the first year Shouguo, the ministers presented the imperial title.

sentences.zh: 是日，即皇帝位。

translations.literal: That day he assumed the imperial throne.
translations.idiomatic: That same day he took the throne.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「遼以賓鐵爲號，取其堅也。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Liao took guest iron as its designation, taking its hardness.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "The Liao styled themselves after guest iron for its hardness.

sentences.zh: 賓鐵雖堅，終亦變壞，惟金不變不壞。

translations.literal: Guest iron, though hard, in the end also changes and breaks; only gold does not change or break.
translations.idiomatic: Guest iron is hard, yet in time it rusts and breaks—only gold endures unchanged.

sentences.zh: 金之色白，完顏部色尚白。

translations.literal: Gold's color is white, and the Wanyan clan esteems white.
translations.idiomatic: Gold is white, and the Wanyan clan holds white in honor.

sentences.zh: 」于是國號大金，改元收國。

translations.literal: Thereupon the state designation was Great Jin, and the era name was changed to Shouguo.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore named the state Great Jin and adopted the era name Shouguo.

sentences.zh: 丙子，上自將攻黃龍府，進臨益州。

translations.literal: On bingzi the emperor personally led the attack on Huanglong Prefecture and advanced to threaten Yi Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On bingzi the emperor led the assault on Huanglong Prefecture and advanced against Yi Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 州人走保黃龍，取其餘民以歸。

translations.literal: The people of the prefecture fled to hold Huanglong; he took the remaining populace and returned.
translations.idiomatic: The prefecture's people fled into Huanglong; he took the rest of the population and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 遼遣都統耶律訛里朵、左副統蕭乙薛、右副統耶律張奴、都監蕭謝佛留，騎二十萬、步卒七萬戍邊。

translations.literal: Liao dispatched Commander-in-Chief Yelü Woliduo, Left Vice Commander Xiao Yixue, Right Vice Commander Yelü Zhangnu, and Inspector Xiao Xiefuliu with two hundred thousand cavalry and seventy thousand infantry to garrison the border.
translations.idiomatic: The Liao sent Commander Yelü Woliduo, Left Vice Commander Xiao Yixue, Right Vice Commander Yelü Zhangnu, and Inspector Xiao Xiefuliu with two hundred thousand horse and seventy thousand foot to hold the frontier.

sentences.zh: 留婁室、銀朮可守黃龍，上率兵趨達魯古城，次甯江州西。

translations.literal: He left Loushi and Yin'aike to guard Huanglong; the emperor led troops toward Dalugu city and halted west of Ningjiang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He left Loushi and Yin'aike to hold Huanglong and marched toward Dalugu, camping west of Ningjiang.

sentences.zh: 遼使僧家奴來議和，國書斥上名，且使爲屬國。

translations.literal: A Liao envoy, Sengjianu, came to negotiate peace; the state letter reproached the emperor by name and demanded that he become a vassal state.
translations.idiomatic: The Liao envoy Sengjianu came to sue for peace. His letter named the emperor disrespectfully and demanded that Jin become a vassal state.

sentences.zh: 庚子，進師，有火光正圓，自空而墜。

translations.literal: On gengzi the army advanced; a perfectly round ball of fire fell from the sky.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi the army marched out. A perfect sphere of fire fell from the sky.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「此祥征，殆天助也！

translations.literal: The emperor said: "This is an auspicious sign—perhaps Heaven aids us!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "This is an omen of fortune—Heaven is helping us!"

sentences.zh: 」酹白水而拜，將士莫不喜躍，進逼達魯古城。

translations.literal: He poured libation on white water and bowed; officers and men all leaped with joy, and advanced to press Dalugu city.
translations.idiomatic: He offered libation on the white water and bowed. Officers and men leaped for joy as the army pressed on toward Dalugu.

sentences.zh: 上登高望遼兵若連雲灌木狀，顧謂左右曰：「遼兵心貳而情怯。

translations.literal: The emperor climbed high and looked; Liao troops were like clouds linked with scrub trees. He turned and said to those beside him: "Liao troops are divided in heart and timid in spirit.
translations.idiomatic: From a height he saw the Liao host spread like scrubland under cloud cover. He told his attendants, "Their hearts are divided and their courage thin.

sentences.zh: 雖多不足畏！

translations.literal: Though many, they are not to be feared!"
translations.idiomatic: However many they are, there is nothing to fear!"

sentences.zh: 」遂趨高阜爲陣。

translations.literal: He then hastened to a high mound and formed battle lines.
translations.idiomatic: He moved his line onto a high mound.

sentences.zh: 宗雄以右翼先馳遼左軍，左軍卻。

translations.literal: Zongxiong with the right wing first charged the Liao left army; the left army gave way.
translations.idiomatic: Zongxiong led the right wing against the Liao left, which fell back.

sentences.zh: 左翼出其陣後，遼右軍皆力戰。

translations.literal: The left wing came out behind their formation; the Liao right army all fought fiercely.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin left swung behind them while the Liao right fought stubbornly.

sentences.zh: 婁室、銀朮可沖其中堅。

translations.literal: Loushi and Yin'aike charged the center.
translations.idiomatic: Loushi and Yin'aike drove into the center.

sentences.zh: 凡九陷陣，皆力戰而出。

translations.literal: Nine times they broke into the enemy lines and each time fought their way out.
translations.idiomatic: Nine times they punched into the enemy line and fought their way out again.

sentences.zh: 宗翰請以中軍助之。

translations.literal: Zonghan requested that the center army assist them.
translations.idiomatic: Zonghan asked to commit the center.

sentences.zh: 上使宗幹往爲疑兵。

translations.literal: The emperor sent Zonggan to serve as a decoy force.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Zonggan to make a diversion.

sentences.zh: 宗雄已得利，擊遼右軍，遼兵遂敗。

translations.literal: Zongxiong had already gained the advantage and struck the Liao right army; the Liao troops then were defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Zongxiong, already gaining the upper hand, smashed the Liao right and the enemy broke.

sentences.zh: 乘勝追躡，至其營，會日已暮，圍之。

translations.literal: Riding victory they pursued to the enemy camp; as the day had already grown dark, they surrounded it.
translations.idiomatic: They pursued to the enemy camp and, as night fell, surrounded it.

sentences.zh: 黎明，遼軍潰圍出，逐北至阿婁岡。

translations.literal: At dawn the Liao army broke out of the encirclement; they pursued north to Alu Ridge.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn the Liao broke out. The pursuit ran north to Alu Ridge.

sentences.zh: 遼步卒盡殪，得其耕具數千以給諸軍。

translations.literal: Liao infantry were all annihilated; they obtained several thousand farming implements and distributed them to the armies.
translations.idiomatic: The Liao foot soldiers were wiped out. Thousands of farming tools were taken and issued to the troops.

sentences.zh: 是役也，遼人本欲屯田，且戰且守，故並其耕具獲之。

translations.literal: In this campaign the Liao had originally intended to establish garrison farming, fighting while holding ground—therefore their farming tools were captured as well.
translations.idiomatic: The Liao had meant to farm while they fought, so their plows and tools were captured along with the men.

sentences.zh: 二月，師還。

translations.literal: In the second month the army returned.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month the army returned.

sentences.zh: 三月辛未朔，獵于寥晦城。

translations.literal: On the first day xinwei of the third month he hunted at Liaohui city.
translations.idiomatic: On the first of the third month, xinwei, he hunted at Liaohui.

sentences.zh: 四月，遼耶律張奴以國書來。

translations.literal: In the fourth month Yelü Zhangnu of Liao came with a state letter.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month Yelü Zhangnu of Liao arrived with a state letter.

sentences.zh: 上以書辭慢侮，留其五人，獨遣張奴回報，書亦如之。

translations.literal: The emperor, because the letter's language was insulting and contemptuous, detained five of them and sent Zhangnu alone back with a reply in the same tone.
translations.idiomatic: Finding the letter insulting, the emperor kept five envoys and sent Zhangnu back alone with an equally contemptuous reply.

sentences.zh: 五月庚午朔，避暑于近郊。

translations.literal: On the first day gengwu of the fifth month he took summer rest in the near suburbs.
translations.idiomatic: On the first of the fifth month, gengwu, he took the summer rest encampment in the near suburbs.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，拜天射柳。

translations.literal: On jiaxu he worshipped Heaven and shot at the willow.
translations.idiomatic: On jiaxu he worshipped Heaven and shot the willow target.

sentences.zh: 故事，五月五日、七月十五日、九月九日拜天射柳，歲以爲常。

translations.literal: By precedent, on the fifth day of the fifth month, the fifteenth of the seventh month, and the ninth of the ninth month they worshipped Heaven and shot at the willow—this was the annual custom.
translations.idiomatic: By custom the court worshipped Heaven and shot the willow on the fifth of the fifth month, the fifteenth of the seventh, and the ninth of the ninth—an annual rite.

sentences.zh: 六月己亥朔，遼耶律張奴復以國書來，猶斥上名。

translations.literal: On the first day jihai of the sixth month Yelü Zhangnu of Liao again came with a state letter, still reproaching the emperor by name.
translations.idiomatic: On the first of the sixth month, jihai, Yelü Zhangnu returned with another letter that still named the emperor disrespectfully.

sentences.zh: 上亦斥遼主名以復之，且諭之使降。

translations.literal: The emperor also reproached the Liao sovereign by name in reply and instructed him to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor answered in kind, naming the Liao ruler, and told him to submit.

sentences.zh: 七月戊辰，以弟吳乞買爲諳班勃極烈，國相撒改爲國論勃極烈。

translations.literal: On the day wuchen of the seventh month his younger brother Wuqimai was made Anban Bojilie and the chief minister Sagai was made Guolun Bojilie.
translations.idiomatic: On wuchen in the seventh month his brother Wuqimai was named Anban Bojilie and Chief Minister Sagai Guolun Bojilie.

sentences.zh: 辭不失爲阿買勃極烈，弟斜也爲國論昊勃極烈，甲戌，遼使辭剌以書來，留之不遣。

translations.literal: Cibushi was made Amai Bojilie and his younger brother Xieye Guolun Hao Bojilie. On jiaxu the Liao envoy Cila came with a letter; he was detained and not sent back.
translations.idiomatic: Cibushi became Amai Bojilie and his brother Xieye Guolun Hao Bojilie. On jiaxu the Liao envoy Cila arrived with a letter and was detained.

sentences.zh: 九百奚營來降。

translations.literal: The Jiubai Xi camp came to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: The Jiubai Xi submitted.

sentences.zh: 八月戊戌，上親征黃龍府。

translations.literal: On the day wuxu of the eighth month the emperor personally campaigned against Huanglong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On wuxu in the eighth month the emperor marched on Huanglong in person.

sentences.zh: 次混同江，無舟，上使一人道前，乘赭白馬徑涉，曰：「視吾鞭所指而行。

translations.literal: He halted at the Huntong River; there were no boats. The emperor sent one man ahead on the path, mounted a reddish-white horse and forded directly, saying: "Watch where my whip points and go that way."
translations.idiomatic: At the Huntong River there were no boats. He sent a man ahead, mounted a reddish-white horse, and rode straight into the current, saying, "Follow where my whip points."

sentences.zh: 」諸軍隨之，水及馬腹。

translations.literal: The armies followed; the water reached the horses' bellies.
translations.idiomatic: The army followed, the water no higher than the horses' bellies.

sentences.zh: 後使舟人測其渡處，深不得其底。

translations.literal: Later boatmen were sent to sound the ford; they could not reach the bottom.
translations.idiomatic: Later boatmen sounded the crossing and could not find the bottom.

sentences.zh: 熙宗天眷二年，以黃龍府爲濟州，軍曰利涉，蓋以太祖涉濟故也。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianjuan under Xizong, Huanglong Prefecture was made Jizhou; the army was called Lisher—this commemorated the Founder's crossing.
translations.idiomatic: In Xizong's second year Tianjuan, Huanglong was renamed Jizhou and its garrison Lisher—the name commemorating this crossing.

sentences.zh: 九月，克黃龍府，遣辭剌還，遂班師。

translations.literal: In the ninth month they captured Huanglong Prefecture, sent Cila back, and withdrew the army.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Huanglong fell. Cila was sent home and the army withdrew.

sentences.zh: 至江，徑渡如前。

translations.literal: Reaching the river, they forded directly as before.
translations.idiomatic: At the river they crossed again as before.

sentences.zh: 丁丑，至自黃龍府。

translations.literal: On dingchou he returned from Huanglong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On dingchou he returned from Huanglong.

sentences.zh: 己卯，黃龍見空中。

translations.literal: On jimao a yellow dragon was seen in the sky.
translations.idiomatic: On jimao a yellow dragon appeared in the sky.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，以國論勃極烈撒改爲國論忽魯勃極烈，阿離合懣爲國論乙室勃極烈。

translations.literal: On guisi Guolun Bojilie Sagai was made Guolun Hulu Bojilie and Alihemen was made Guolun Yishi Bojilie.
translations.idiomatic: On guisi Sagai was promoted to Guolun Hulu Bojilie and Alihemen to Guolun Yishi Bojilie.

sentences.zh: 十一月，遼主聞取黃龍府，大懼，自將七十萬至駝門。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month the Liao sovereign, hearing that Huanglong Prefecture had been taken, was greatly afraid and personally led seven hundred thousand to Tuomen.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, hearing that Huanglong had fallen, the Liao emperor was terrified and marched in person with seven hundred thousand men to Tuomen.

sentences.zh: 附馬蕭特末、林牙蕭查剌等騎五萬、步四十萬至斡鄰濼。

translations.literal: The imperial son-in-law Xiao Temu, Linya Xiao Zhala, and others with fifty thousand cavalry and four hundred thousand infantry reached Wolun Marsh.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial son-in-law Xiao Temu, Linya Xiao Zhala, and others brought fifty thousand horse and four hundred thousand foot to Wolun Marsh.

sentences.zh: 上自將御之。

translations.literal: The emperor personally led the force to meet them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor led the army out to meet them in person.

sentences.zh: 十二月己亥，行次爻剌，會諸將議。

translations.literal: On the day jihai of the twelfth month, marching and halting at Yaola, he convened the generals for deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: On jihai in the twelfth month, camped at Yaola, he called his commanders to council.

sentences.zh: 皆曰：「遼兵號七十萬，其鋒未易當。

translations.literal: All said: "Liao troops are said to number seven hundred thousand; their edge is not easy to withstand.
translations.idiomatic: All said, "The Liao claim seven hundred thousand men. Their spearhead will not be easy to meet.

sentences.zh: 吾軍遠來。

translations.literal: Our army has come from afar.
translations.idiomatic: Our army has marched far.

sentences.zh: 人馬疲乏，宜駐于此，深溝高壘以待。

translations.literal: Men and horses are weary; we should halt here, dig deep ditches and raise high ramparts, and wait."
translations.idiomatic: Men and horses are exhausted. We should camp here, dig in behind deep ditches and high walls, and wait."

sentences.zh: 」上從之。

translations.literal: The emperor agreed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 遣迪古乃、銀朮可鎮達魯古。

translations.literal: He sent Digunai and Yin'aike to garrison Dalugu.
translations.idiomatic: He left Digunai and Yin'aike to hold Dalugu.

sentences.zh: 丁未，上以騎兵親候遼軍，獲督餉者，知遼主以張奴叛，西還二日矣。

translations.literal: On dingwei the emperor with cavalry personally reconnoitered the Liao army, captured a grain-supply officer, and learned that the Liao sovereign, because Zhangnu had rebelled, had already returned west two days before.
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei he rode out with cavalry to scout the Liao host, seized a supply officer, and learned that the Liao emperor had turned west two days earlier after Zhangnu's rebellion.

sentences.zh: 是日，上還至熟結濼，有光見于予端。

translations.literal: That day the emperor returned to Shujie Marsh; a light was seen at the tip of his bow.
translations.idiomatic: That day, returning to Shujie Marsh, a light appeared at the tip of his bow.

sentences.zh: 戊申，諸將曰：「今遼主既還，可乘怠追擊之。

translations.literal: On wushen the generals said: "Now that the Liao sovereign has returned, we can take advantage of their slackness and pursue and strike them."
translations.idiomatic: On wushen the commanders said, "The Liao emperor has withdrawn—we can strike while they are weary."

sentences.zh: 」上曰「敵來不迎戰，去而追之，欲以此爲勇邪？

translations.literal: The emperor said: "When the enemy came you did not go out to fight; when they leave you pursue—do you wish to make this your courage?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "You would not fight when they came, yet you chase them when they leave—is that what you call courage?"

sentences.zh: 」衆皆悚愧，願自效。

translations.literal: All were fearful and ashamed, and wished to exert themselves.
translations.idiomatic: They were stricken with shame and begged to prove themselves.

sentences.zh: 上復曰：「誠欲追敵，約齎以往，無事餫饋。

translations.literal: The emperor again said: "If you truly wish to pursue the enemy, travel with rations packed—there is no need for supply trains.
translations.idiomatic: He added, "If you mean to pursue, march with rations in your packs—no supply train.

sentences.zh: 若破敵，何求不得。

translations.literal: If you break the enemy, what could you not obtain?"
translations.idiomatic: Break the enemy and you will lack for nothing."

sentences.zh: 」衆皆奮躍，追及遼主于護步答岡。

translations.literal: All leaped with ardor and overtook the Liao sovereign at Hubuda Ridge.
translations.idiomatic: They sprang to the chase and caught the Liao emperor at Hubuda Ridge.

sentences.zh: 是役也，兵止二萬。

translations.literal: In this campaign the troops numbered only twenty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: In this battle he had only twenty thousand men.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「彼衆我寡，兵不可分。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "They are many and we few—the army must not be divided.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "They outnumber us. Do not split the army.

sentences.zh: 視其中軍最堅，遼主必在焉。

translations.literal: Look—their center army is strongest; the Liao sovereign must be there.
translations.idiomatic: Their center is the strongest—that is where the Liao emperor will be.

sentences.zh: 敗其中軍，可以得志。

translations.literal: Defeat the center army and you can achieve your aim."
translations.idiomatic: Break the center and you will have your victory."

sentences.zh: 」使右翼先戰。

translations.literal: He had the right wing fight first.
translations.idiomatic: He sent the right wing in first.

sentences.zh: 兵數交，左翼合而攻之。

translations.literal: When the forces had joined battle, the left wing united and attacked.
translations.idiomatic: Once the lines met, the left wing closed and struck.

sentences.zh: 遼兵大潰，我師馳之，橫出其中。

translations.literal: Liao troops collapsed in great disorder; our army galloped after them and cut across through their midst.
translations.idiomatic: The Liao broke. Our cavalry swept through their center.

sentences.zh: 遼師敗績，死者相屬百餘里。

translations.literal: The Liao army suffered a crushing defeat; the dead stretched in succession for more than a hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: The dead lay heaped for more than a hundred li.

sentences.zh: 獲輿輦帟幄兵械軍資，他寶物馬牛不可勝計。

translations.literal: They captured chariots, imperial carriages, curtains, tents, weapons, military stores, and other precious objects, horses, and cattle beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: They took chariots, imperial wagons, tents, arms, stores, treasure, horses, and cattle beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 是戰，斜也援矛殺數十人，阿離本被圍，溫蒂罕迪忽迭以四謀克兵出之，完顏蒙刮身被數創，力戰不已，功皆論最。

translations.literal: In this battle Xieye with spear in hand killed several tens of men; Aliben was surrounded and Wendihan Dihudie with four mouke of troops rescued him; Wanyan Menggua received several wounds on his body yet fought on without cease—all their merits were ranked highest.
translations.idiomatic: In this fight Xieye killed dozens with his spear. Aliben was surrounded until Wendihan Dihudie broke in with four mouke. Wanyan Menggua took wound after wound yet kept fighting. All were ranked highest in merit.

sentences.zh: 蕭特末等焚營遁去，遂班師。

translations.literal: Xiao Temu and others burned their camp and fled; the army then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Temu burned his camp and fled. The army withdrew.

sentences.zh: 來穀撒喝取開州，婆盧火下特鄰城，辭里罕降。

translations.literal: Laigusahuo took Kai Prefecture; Boluhuo reduced Telin city; Cilihan surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Laigusahuo took Kai Prefecture, Boluhuo took Telin, and Cilihan submitted.

sentences.zh: 二年正月戊子，詔曰：「自破遼兵，四方來降者衆，宜加優恤。

translations.literal: On the day wuzi of the first month of the second year an edict said: "Since defeating Liao troops, those coming to surrender from the four directions are many; they should receive added favor and relief.
translations.idiomatic: On wuzi in the first month of the second year an edict declared, "Since we broke the Liao, submissions have poured in from every quarter. Treat them generously.

sentences.zh: 自今契丹、奚、漢、渤海、系遼籍女直、室韋、達魯古、兀惹、鐵驪諸部官民，己降或爲軍所俘獲，逃遁而還者，勿以爲罪。

translations.literal: From now on among Khitan, Xi, Han, Bohai, Jurchen registered under Liao, Shiwei, Dalugu, Wunai, Tieli, and all other tribes—officials and commoners who have already surrendered or were captured by the army, or who fled and have returned—do not treat them as guilty.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth among Khitan, Xi, Han, Bohai, Jurchen on Liao rolls, Shiwei, Dalugu, Wunai, Tieli, and all other peoples—whether they have submitted, been captured, or fled and returned—none shall be punished.

sentences.zh: 其酋長仍官之，且使從宜居處。」

translations.literal: Their chiefs shall still hold office, and they shall be allowed to settle where it suits them."
translations.idiomatic: Their chiefs shall keep their offices and settle where they choose."

sentences.zh: 閏月，高永昌據東京，使撻不野來求援。

translations.literal: In the intercalary month Gao Yongchang held the Eastern Capital and sent Tabuye to request aid.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary month Gao Yongchang seized the Eastern Capital and sent Tabuye to ask for aid.

sentences.zh: 高麗遣使來賀捷，且求保州。

translations.literal: Goryeo dispatched envoys to congratulate on the victory and also requested Bozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Goryeo sent envoys to congratulate him on his victories and to ask for Bozhou.

sentences.zh: 詔許自取之。

translations.literal: An edict permitted them to take it themselves.
translations.idiomatic: He decreed that they might take it themselves.

sentences.zh: 二月己巳，詔曰：「比以歲凶，庶民艱食，多依附豪族，因爲奴隸，及有犯法，征償莫辦，折身爲奴者，或私約立限，以人對贖，過期則爲奴者，並聽以兩人贖一爲良。

translations.literal: On the day jisi of the second month an edict said: "Recently because years have been bad, the common people have had scant food and many have attached themselves to powerful families and become slaves. When some violated the law and could not pay fines levied against them, they sold themselves into slavery; some privately set terms to redeem with persons—if the term expired they became slaves. All are permitted to redeem one as a commoner with two persons."
translations.idiomatic: On jisi in the second month an edict said, "In these lean years many commoners, starving, have bound themselves to great families as slaves. Some sold themselves to pay fines; some agreed private terms to redeem with kin, and when the term expired remained slaves. Let any such person be freed as a commoner if two others stand surety for one."

sentences.zh: 若元約以一人贖者，即從元約。

translations.literal: If the original agreement was to redeem with one person, follow the original agreement.
translations.idiomatic: Where the original agreement was one for one, that agreement shall stand.

sentences.zh: 」四月乙丑，以斡魯統內外諸軍，與蒲察、迪古乃會咸州路都統斡魯古討高永昌。

translations.literal: On yichou of the fourth month Wolu was placed in command of all armies within and without, and with Pucha and Digunai joined Xianzhou Circuit Commander-in-Chief Wulugu to campaign against Gao Yongchang.
translations.idiomatic: On yichou in the fourth month Wolu took command of all forces at home and abroad, and with Pucha and Digunai joined Wulugu, commander of Xianzhou circuit, to campaign against Gao Yongchang.

sentences.zh: 胡沙補等被害。

translations.literal: Hushabu and others were killed.
translations.idiomatic: Hushabu and others were killed.

sentences.zh: 五月，斡魯等敗永昌，撻不野擒永昌以獻，戮之于軍。
